title: Tanghua (hot sugar drawing)
summary: Tanghua is the Chinese street art of drawing with hot syrup. The maker lets a thin thread of melted sugar run from a small ladle onto a cold stone slab, tracing the outline of a flower, bird or animal and filling it with swirls and zigzags, then lifts the cooled figure on a bamboo stick.
howToPlay: Pick a colour of sugar and a stroke from the strip under the slab: waves, curls, zigzags, leaves, rings and drops.
Tap a square to lay the stroke: its mirror image appears on the other side of the figure, as in a symmetrical drawing.
Copy the small figure above the slab, then press Check.
rules: The slab is mirrored left to right, so every figure has two matching halves.
A square scores only when its stroke and its shade of sugar both match the figure.
Laying the same stroke and shade again, or using the eraser, clears the square.
Three stars need a near-perfect copy; undo and clear are free.
heritageNote: Sugar drawing is known from Sichuan and many other parts of China, where street makers still draw figures for passers-by; it is recognised as intangible cultural heritage in several provinces.
